howTo.title: How to read
items: Red dates are Sundays and public holidays; blue dates are Saturdays.
In the monthly calendar, small numbers under dates are lunar dates, with solar terms and traditional days noted.
Save holidays to your phone or Google Calendar in one go with the .ics file.
To find where annual leave gives the longest break, use the holiday planner.

items.q: How many public holidays does Korea have in 2027?
items.a: 24 days, including 7 substitute holidays (Seollal, Labor Day, Constitution Day, Liberation Day, National Foundation Day, Hangeul Day, Christmas). 15 of them fall on weekdays. With 104 weekend days that's 119 days off, one fewer than 2026 (120).
Feb 6 (Sat) to Feb 8 (Mon). Because the break overlaps a weekend, Feb 9 (Tue) is a substitute holiday, so Feb 6–9 are off.
Sep 14 (Tue) to 16 (Thu). Taking leave on the 13th and 17th gives nine days off, Sep 11 to 19.

items.q: Which days are substitute holidays in 2027?
items.a: Feb 9 (Seollal), May 3 (Labor Day), Jul 19 (Constitution Day), Aug 16 (Liberation Day), Oct 4 (National Foundation Day), Oct 11 (Hangeul Day) and Dec 27 (Christmas).

items.q: Are Labor Day and Constitution Day holidays?
items.a: Yes. A 2026 amendment of the Regulations on Public Holidays made Labor Day (May 1) and Constitution Day (Jul 17) public holidays. Both fall on Saturdays in 2027, so May 3 and Jul 19 are substitute holidays.

items.q: How are the 24 solar terms set?
items.a: The sun's path (the ecliptic) is divided every 15°, giving 24 terms a year. Dates and times follow KASI calendar data (KST): Start of Spring Feb 4 10:46, Summer Solstice Jun 21 23:11, Winter Solstice Dec 22 11:42.
Chobok Jul 20, Jungbok Jul 30, Malbok Aug 9. The First Full Moon is Feb 21 and Dano is Jun 9.

items.q: Can I print it or save a PDF?
items.a: 'Print year' fits 12 months on one landscape A4 page; 'Print months' prints each month large with lunar dates, holidays and solar terms. Choose 'Save as PDF' in the print dialog to get a file.
